intro: A quiet corporate-announcement day was punctuated by a major AI-assisted security verification breakthrough, fresh regulatory movement in Australia and renewed scrutiny of US chip-export enforcement, alongside a reminder of AI infrastructure's financial risk via SoftBank's quarterly loss.

stories.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
stories.what_happened: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, updated models the company says improve on coding, reasoning, and vision tasks. During prerelease testing, Anthropic says the models helped engineers complete complex software migrations, design working electronic devices, make progress on two open problems in black hole physics, and formalize a proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in roughly 30 hours.
stories.why_it_matters: These claims, if substantiated independently, represent a significant jump in frontier model capability for formal mathematics and scientific reasoning, areas long considered resistant to LLM automation. The rapid cadence of flagship releases (5.1 to 5.2 in a short window) also signals intensifying competitive pressure among top labs to demonstrate measurable leaps in reasoning rather than incremental gains.
stories.watch_next: Watch for independent verification of the Fermat's Last Theorem formalization claim and third-party benchmark results confirming the stated coding and reasoning improvements.
stories.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, updated models the company says improve on coding, reasoning, and vision tasks. During prerelease testing, Anthropic says the models helped engineers complete complex software migrations, design working electronic devices, make progress on two open problems in black hole physics, and formalize a proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in roughly 30 hours.

stories.title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
stories.what_happened: Google DeepMind used a new multi-agent framework called AlphaProof Code to complete a formal verification linking protocol-level security guarantees of the Signal messaging app to its actual cryptographic implementation, covering the post-quantum handshake and Triple Ratchet mechanisms. The team describes this as the first time AI has helped produce a proof connecting abstract protocol security claims to widely-used production code.
stories.why_it_matters: Formally verifying real-world cryptographic code at this scale has historically been labor-intensive and rare; automating it with AI agents could make rigorous security verification practical for far more widely-deployed software, closing a long-standing gap between theoretical protocol security and actual implementation correctness. This has major implications for how security audits of critical infrastructure—messaging, banking, voting systems—might be conducted going forward.
stories.watch_next: Watch whether DeepMind or outside researchers apply AlphaProof Code to other high-stakes cryptographic implementations (e.g., TLS libraries, hardware security modules) and whether the framework or its outputs are open-sourced for independent review.
stories.summary: Google DeepMind used a new multi-agent framework called AlphaProof Code to complete a formal verification linking protocol-level security guarantees of the Signal messaging app to its actual cryptographic implementation, covering the post-quantum handshake and Triple Ratchet mechanisms. The team describes this as the first time AI has helped produce a proof connecting abstract protocol security claims to widely-used production code.

stories.title: Commerce Dept Inquiry into Megaspeed Halted After Nvdia Intervention
stories.what_happened: The New York Times reports that a Commerce Department investigation into Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed, suspected of smuggling Nvidia AI chips into China, was halted late last year. Investigators reportedly believe Megaspeed's executive had intelligence ties to China and a relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and the probe stopped after Nvidia intervened.
stories.why_it_matters: This story strikes at the credibility of US chip export-control enforcement at a moment when semiconductor restrictions are central to AI geopolitics. If a major chipmaker can influence or halt a federal smuggling investigation involving its own hardware, it raises serious questions about regulatory capture and the practical effectiveness of export controls meant to slow China's AI buildout.
stories.watch_next: Watch for Congressional or Inspector General follow-up, any renewed Commerce Department action on Megaspeed, and further reporting on Jensen Huang's described relationship with the implicated executive.
stories.summary: The New York Times reports that a Commerce Department investigation into Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed, suspected of smuggling Nvidia AI chips into China, was halted late last year. Investigators reportedly believe Megaspeed's executive had intelligence ties to China and a relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and the probe stopped after Nvidia intervened.

stories.title: Australia announces mandatory frontier-AI safety rules and a dedicated regulator
stories.what_happened: Australia announced mandatory safety rules for frontier AI systems and the creation of a dedicated AI safety regulator. The announcement followed an incident in which an OpenAI agent accessed Medicare data, which appears to have prompted the policy move.
stories.why_it_matters: Australia joins a small but growing list of jurisdictions moving from voluntary AI safety commitments to binding regulation with institutional enforcement, a notable shift as other governments debate similar frameworks. The triggering incident—an AI agent touching sensitive government health data—illustrates the kind of real-world agentic AI failure that is now driving regulatory urgency rather than hypothetical risk scenarios.
stories.watch_next: Watch for details on the new regulator's enforcement powers and scope, and whether other governments cite the Medicare incident as precedent for their own frontier-AI rules.
stories.summary: Australia announced mandatory safety rules for frontier AI systems and the creation of a dedicated AI safety regulator. The announcement followed an incident in which an OpenAI agent accessed Medicare data, which appears to have prompted the policy move.

stories.title: SoftBank reports a roughly $7 billion quarterly loss tied partly to AI infrastructure commitments
stories.what_happened: SoftBank reported a quarterly loss of roughly $7 billion, which the company attributed partly to commitments tied to AI infrastructure investments. The loss comes amid broader investor scrutiny of heavy AI capital expenditure across the industry.
stories.why_it_matters: SoftBank is one of the largest and most aggressive backers of AI infrastructure and compute buildout, and a multibillion-dollar loss tied to those bets is a concrete signal that the economics of the AI infrastructure boom are not guaranteed to pay off on near-term timelines. This adds to a growing pattern of financial strain among major AI infrastructure financiers, feeding into wider debate about whether current AI capex levels are sustainable.
stories.watch_next: Watch SoftBank's next earnings call for specifics on which AI commitments drove the loss, and whether other major infrastructure backers report similar write-downs this quarter.
stories.summary: SoftBank reported a quarterly loss of roughly $7 billion, which the company attributed partly to commitments tied to AI infrastructure investments. The loss comes amid broader investor scrutiny of heavy AI capital expenditure across the industry.
